# slangc -v version string can be cosmetically stale after a ToT rebuild (cached git-describe stamp)

**Symptom:** After `git reset --hard origin/master` to a new ToT and rebuilding `slangc` (incremental, same `build/Debug/bin/slangc` path), `slangc -v` still printed the OLD describe string (e.g. `2026.10.2-33-g5230a81f2`) even though the binary was genuinely built from current ToT (HEAD `6fac3e6d0`).

**Cause:** `slang-tag-version.h` (the git-describe stamp consumed by `-v`) is generated by a CMake custom command that runs at *configure* time and is cached; an incremental `cmake --build` after a plain `git reset` does not necessarily re-run it. So the version *string* lags the actual source.

**Do NOT trust `-v` to confirm a rebuild picked up ToT.** Instead verify the binary is current by behavior/source, e.g.:
- `git describe --tags` at HEAD vs the string (mismatch = stale string, not stale binary);
- diff a relevant source file vs the old commit (`git log --oneline <old>..HEAD -- <file>`), and check the binary's mtime is newer than the source mtime (relinked);
- exercise a ToT-only flag the old binary wouldn't accept (e.g. flags added by a recent PR) — exit 0 proves the new code is in.

**To refresh the string** (only if you actually need it correct): re-run `cmake --preset ...` (reconfigure) or delete `build/source/slang/slang-version-header/slang-tag-version.h` before building. For read-only repro work the cosmetic staleness is harmless once you've confirmed the binary is ToT by other means.
